table.name: circuits
table.purpose: One row per motor racing circuit (Formula 1 venues): its identifier, names, location, country, geographic coordinates, and Wikipedia link. 72 circuits, matching the classic F1 circuits dataset (e.g. Ergast).

col_001.name: circuit_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier of the circuit (values 2-73).

col_002.name: circuit_ref
col_002.description: Unique short slug/reference name of the circuit (lowercase, e.g. 'ricard', 'zolder', 'interlagos'), used as a textual key.

col_003.name: circuit_name
col_003.description: Full display name of the circuit (e.g. 'Circuit Paul Ricard', 'Silverstone Circuit').

col_004.name: location
col_004.description: Town/city or locality where the circuit is situated (e.g. 'Le Castellet', 'Heusden-Zolder'); slightly non-unique (69 distinct).

col_006.name: latitude
col_006.description: Latitude of the circuit in decimal degrees (range -34.9 to 57.3).

col_007.name: longitude
col_007.description: Longitude of the circuit in decimal degrees (range -118.2 to 138.9).

col_009.name: wikipedia_url
col_009.description: Wikipedia article URL for the circuit.

table.purpose: t02 is a fact/detail table keyed by col_001; each row links a parent entity (col_002, referencing t09/t10/t11) and a secondary entity (col_003, referencing t04/t05/t06), with a small numeric measure (col_004). The exact business domain cannot be determined from the data alone.

col_001.name: row_id
col_001.description: Primary key of t02; unique surrogate identifier (1..15579) for each row. Referenced as a foreign key by many other tables (t03, t05, t07, t08, t09, t10, t11), so it identifies an entity other tables attach to.

col_002.name: parent_entity_id
col_002.description: Foreign key referencing the primary key of t09, t10 and t11 (which appear to share the same id space, 907 distinct values). Groups rows ~20 per value, so it identifies the parent entity each row belongs to.

col_003.name: category_entity_id
col_003.description: Foreign key referencing the primary key of t04, t05 and t06 (shared id space, 172 distinct values). A secondary classification/dimension for the row; the exact meaning of the referenced entity is unknown.

col_004.name: quantity
col_004.description: Small non-negative numeric measure (0..66, mostly 0, integer-valued). Likely a count or quantity associated with the row; units and exact meaning unresolved.

table.purpose: Unresolved. The table has 11,836 rows keyed by a surrogate id (col_001) that is referenced by many other tables (t05, t07–t11), suggesting it is a central fact/entity table (e.g., line items or transactions). Each row appears to belong to one of 906 groups (col_002), and the rows are further partitioned into 22 evenly-sized batches (col_005/col_006, ~906 rows each). Without access to the referenced tables' contents, the domain cannot be determined. Its columns are documented below under their original keys.

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Surrogate primary key of the table; unique integer from 1 to 26,872 with no gaps in sequence meaning. Referenced (many_to_one) by columns in t05, t07, t08, t09, t10 and t11, so other tables point at rows of this table.

col_002.name: group_id
col_002.description: Foreign key grouping the 11,836 rows into 906 groups (each group has ~13 rows on average; top groups have ~20-22 rows). References t02.col_001, t09.col_001 and t10.col_001. Likely the parent entity these rows belong to (e.g., an order, invoice, or account), but the exact meaning is unresolved because the referenced tables' contents are unknown.

col_003.name: category_id
col_003.description: Foreign key to a small lookup/classification table (156 distinct values, 1-210, skewed: value 6 covers 903 rows). References t02.col_001, t04.col_001 and t05.col_001. Probably a category/type code for the row, but the specific meaning cannot be determined from the evidence.

col_004.name: amount
col_004.description: Continuous numeric measure, 0.0 to 765.0, with 0.0 as the most common value (3,800 rows, 32%) and values in half-steps (27.5, 72.5). Plausibly a monetary amount (price, fee, or charge) where zero is common. Units and exact meaning unresolved.

col_005.name: batch_number
col_005.description: Integer 1-22 with 22 distinct values, each occurring ~906 times — i.e., exactly one value per col_002 group, so it is constant within each group and partitions the table into 22 equal slices. Declared BIGINT. Could be a period (e.g., month), a batch, or a denormalized group attribute. Duplicated by col_006. Exact meaning unresolved.

col_006.name: batch_number_text
col_006.description: Character-typed copy of col_005: identical values (1-22, same distribution, same joins). A redundant duplicate of col_005 stored as VARCHAR. Same unresolved meaning as col_005.

col_007.name: count
col_007.description: Small non-negative integer, 0-19, heavily skewed to 0 (9,272 rows, 78%). Reads like a count of something (items, events, retries) that is usually zero. The joins reported are almost certainly coincidental value overlaps with small lookup tables, not real relationships. Exact meaning unresolved.

table.name: constructors
table.purpose: Formula 1 constructors (racing teams/builders). One row per constructor, referenced by many other tables (results, qualifying, races, etc.).

col_001.name: constructor_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique surrogate identifier for the constructor, referenced by many other tables.

col_002.name: constructor_ref
col_002.description: Unique short slug/reference code for the constructor (lowercase, URL-friendly, e.g. 'tyrrell', 'tec-mec').

col_003.name: name
col_003.description: Full display name of the constructor (e.g. 'Alfa Romeo', 'Brabham-Repco').

col_004.name: nationality
col_004.description: Constructor's nationality as an adjective (British, American, Italian, ...).

table.purpose: t05 appears to be a transactional/fact table: each row is one event or line item, identified by a unique surrogate key (col_001) that is referenced by many other tables (t02, t03, t07–t11), with several foreign keys to dimension-like tables and two numeric measures. The exact business domain cannot be determined from the data alone.

col_001.name: row_id
col_001.description: Primary key / unique surrogate identifier of the row. Values are unique integers from 1 to 68460 (31578 present), with no inherent meaning. Referenced by many other tables (t02, t03, t07, t08, t09, t10, t11), confirming it is the row's identifier used by child/detail tables.

col_002.name: dimension_a_id
col_002.description: Integer foreign key (1–982) referencing a parent entity in t02/t09/t10 (all share the same key column). Likely a dimension such as customer, account, or organization. The specific entity is unresolved.

col_003.name: dimension_b_id
col_003.description: Integer foreign key (1–841) referencing a parent entity in t02/t06/t09. A second dimension key, distinct from col_002 (e.g. product, store, or category). Specific entity unresolved.

col_004.name: amount
col_004.description: Numeric measure, non-negative float (0–397). Over half the rows are 0.0, and values are mostly small integers or half-integers (e.g. 27.5). Plausibly a quantity, count, or monetary amount. Units and exact meaning unresolved.

col_005.name: dimension_c_id
col_005.description: Integer foreign key (1–108) referencing t02/t03/t06. Each value appears exactly 970 times, suggesting a balanced grouping (e.g. period, region, or category with 108 members). Specific entity unresolved.

col_006.name: dimension_c_id_text
col_006.description: Text-stored duplicate of col_005: identical distribution (1–108, each value 970 times) and same joins. Same dimension as col_005, stored as VARCHAR. Possibly a denormalized copy or a code/label field that happens to hold the same numbers.

table.name: drivers
table.purpose: One row per racing driver (Formula 1 style database): unique driver id, name, date of birth, nationality and Wikipedia link. Referenced by many other tables (results, qualifying, etc.) via the driver id.

col_001.name: driver_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric driver identifier, 1-840, referenced by many other tables.

col_002.name: driver_ref
col_002.description: Unique driver reference slug (surname-based, e.g. 'bonnier', 'gilles_villeneuve'), used as a stable textual key.

col_003.name: driver_number
col_003.description: Permanent driver race number; null for ~96% of drivers (only recent-era drivers have permanent numbers). Values 2-99.

col_004.name: driver_code
col_004.description: Three-letter driver abbreviation (e.g. VER, ROS, MAG) used in timing screens; null for most drivers.

col_008.name: nationality
col_008.description: Driver's nationality as an adjective (British, American, Italian, ...).

col_009.name: wikipedia_url
col_009.description: Wikipedia article URL for the driver; empty string when no article exists.

table.name: lap_times
table.purpose: One row per lap completed by a driver in a race: the driver's position and lap time for each lap of each race (F1-style lap times data).

col_001.name: race_id
col_001.description: Identifier of the race (references a races table, e.g. t02/t09/t10). 389 distinct races, each appearing thousands of times (one row per driver-lap).

col_002.name: driver_id
col_002.description: Identifier of the driver completing the lap (references a drivers table, e.g. t06). 121 distinct drivers.

col_003.name: lap_number
col_003.description: Lap number within the race, 1-78. Roughly uniform counts per lap number, consistent with all drivers recording a time each lap.

col_004.name: position
col_004.description: Driver's race position at the end of that lap, 1-24, with near-uniform counts across positions.

col_005.name: lap_time
col_005.description: Lap time formatted as m:ss.mmm (e.g. '1:23.794' = 1 minute 23.794 seconds).

col_006.name: lap_time_ms
col_006.description: Same lap time in milliseconds (e.g. 83794 ms = 1:23.794); numeric counterpart of col_005.

table.purpose: Likely a transactional/event table where each row records an occurrence (e.g., a booking, trip, or scheduled event) with a time-of-day, a small categorical code, and a monetary-style amount. The exact domain cannot be determined from the data alone; the joins point to several lookup tables (t02, t03, t05, t09, t10) whose contents are not shown, so the entity type remains unresolved.

col_003.description: Small ordinal code 1-6 with a strongly skewed distribution (1 most common, 6 rare). Plausibly a rank/class/grade (e.g., service class, priority, or day-of-week-like category). References t02/t03/t04. The exact meaning is not supported by the evidence.

col_005.name: time_of_day
col_005.description: Time of day in HH:MM:SS format, high cardinality (4872 distinct), values spread across the day. Clearly a time-of-day field, though whether it is a scheduled or actual event time cannot be distinguished.

col_006.name: amount
col_006.description: Decimal value stored as text, range ~12.9-59.6 with median ~23.3. Its values are exactly col_007 divided by 1000, so it is the same quantity expressed with 3 decimal places. Plausibly a price/fare or a rate, but the unit and meaning are not confirmed; the joins to t02/t03/t05 are likely coincidental numeric matches.

col_007.name: amount_scaled
col_007.description: Integer equal to col_006 * 1000 for the vast majority of rows (e.g., 30.888 -> 30888), i.e., the same quantity expressed in thousandths. A few larger values (up to ~2,011,266) do not match col_006, suggesting either outliers or a partially different quantity. Meaning of the underlying amount is unresolved.

table.name: qualifying_results
table.purpose: One row per driver per race qualifying session (F1-style): the driver, car number, grid/qualifying position and their Q1/Q2/Q3 lap times. The pattern of three time columns with increasing null rates (Q1 nearly always set, Q2 only for those who progress, Q3 only for the top ten) strongly matches a three-segment qualifying format.

col_001.name: qualifying_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique row identifier (surrogate id).

col_002.name: race_id
col_002.description: Reference to the races table (t02/t10/t11). 339 distinct races, ~22 rows each, matching one row per driver per race.

col_003.name: driver_id
col_003.description: Reference to the drivers table (t02/t06/t11). 151 distinct drivers.

col_004.name: constructor_id
col_004.description: Reference to the constructors/teams table (t02/t04/t05). 41 distinct teams.

col_005.name: car_number
col_005.description: Driver's car number for the session (0-99, small distinct set).

col_006.name: qualifying_position
col_006.description: Finishing position in qualifying, 1-28, roughly uniform (each value ~339 times = one per race), consistent with grid position.

col_007.name: q1_time
col_007.description: Q1 lap time in m:ss.mmm format (e.g. 1:31.470). Set for ~98% of rows, as every driver runs Q1.

col_008.name: q2_time
col_008.description: Q2 lap time in m:ss.mmm format. Present for ~49% of rows, matching drivers who advance past Q1.

col_009.name: q3_time
col_009.description: Q3 lap time in m:ss.mmm format. Present for ~29% of rows, matching only the top-ten shootout participants.

table.name: races
table.purpose: One row per Formula 1 Grand Prix race (1950–2017), with its year, round, circuit, name, date, start time, and Wikipedia URL. Referenced by results/qualifying/lap-times style tables (t02, t03, t05, t07, t08, t09, t11).

col_001.name: race_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier for each race. Referenced by many other tables (results, qualifying, etc.).

col_002.name: year
col_002.description: Race season year (1950–2017); also references a seasons/year lookup table (t02, t09, t11).

col_003.name: round
col_003.description: Round number of the race within its season (1–21); each value appears ~68 times, consistent with one race per round per season.

col_004.name: circuit_id
col_004.description: Reference to the circuit (t05) where the race was held; 72 distinct circuits.

col_005.name: race_name
col_005.description: Official name of the Grand Prix, e.g. 'British Grand Prix', 'Monaco Grand Prix'.

col_006.name: race_date
col_006.description: Date the race was held (1950-05-13 to 2017-11-26), unique per row.

col_007.name: race_time
col_007.description: Scheduled start time of the race (HH:MM:SS, likely UTC); null for 75% of rows, mostly older races where start time is unknown.

col_008.name: wiki_url
col_008.description: Wikipedia URL for the race article; unique per row.

table.purpose: Unresolved. The row shape (a unique id, several foreign keys to other tables, a sparse text field with values like '+0.7' / '+8:22.19' that look like margins or deltas, a sparse time-like field '1:34.091' (min:sec.millis), a sparse numeric field around 90-257, and a sparse large integer around 1.5M-15M) strongly suggests per-participant results in a timed competition, likely racing-style events (e.g. horse or motor racing), where only some rows (finishers/placegetters) carry the timing fields. However, no table or column names confirm the domain, so the table's exact meaning stays unresolved. Columns that are pure integer foreign keys into other opaque tables cannot be named beyond their structural role.

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Primary key of the table; unique integer identifier for each row (each result/entry).

col_008.description: Text code, 39 distinct values; 'R' dominates (8495 rows) with 'F' (1368) and numeric-string values. 'R'/'F' plausibly stand for status flags (e.g. Racing/Finished, or Result/Fall in a racing context), but the evidence does not settle the meaning.

col_009.description: Small-range integer (1-39) referencing another table; its values largely mirror col_008's numeric values, suggesting it is the numeric counterpart of the col_008 code, but this is unconfirmed.

col_012.name: margin_or_delta
col_012.description: Sparse (25% populated) text values like '+0.7', '+8:22.19', '+24.160'. The '+' prefix and mixed formats (plain number vs min:sec) suggest a margin/deficit relative to a reference (e.g. gap behind a leader/winner), but the unit and exact semantics are unconfirmed.

col_016.name: finish_time
col_016.description: Sparse (22% populated) text in 'm:ss.mmm' format (e.g. '1:34.091', '1:21.134'), i.e. a duration of roughly 1-2 minutes. Very likely a finish/elapsed time, but the exact event is unknown.

col_017.description: Sparse (22% populated) decimal 89.5-257.3, median ~202, stored as text. Could be an average speed or another derived performance metric; units unconfirmed.

table.name: seasons
table.purpose: One row per Formula One season (1950-2017), with a link to its Wikipedia article. Likely a dimension/lookup table for F1 seasons referenced by other tables (e.g. races, results).

col_001.name: season_year
col_001.description: Year of the Formula One season (1950-2017), one row per year; primary key of the table.

col_002.name: wikipedia_url
col_002.description: URL of the Wikipedia article for that season's Formula One championship (e.g. http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Formula_One_season).

table.name: status
table.purpose: Lookup table of Formula 1 race non-finish classifications/status codes: each row is a distinct reason a driver did not finish (or finished laps behind), e.g. mechanical failures or '+N Laps'. Likely a 'status' table keyed by statusId, referenced by race results tables (t01–t12).

col_001.name: status_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique integer identifier for each non-finish/finish status code.

col_002.name: status_label
col_002.description: Human-readable status description: either a mechanical/technical failure reason (e.g. 'Engine', 'Out of fuel', 'Water pipe') or a laps-behind indicator ('+1 Lap', '+30 Laps').
